product_backlog.summary: This epic covers building the core YAML-based plugin system. It includes loading plugins, parsing rule definitions (including versioned rules), applying both structured report parsers and log scrapers, and handling different aggregation modes. This is the foundational component that enables Kronograf to be tool-agnostic.
product_backlog.title: Implement the core Plugin Engine
product_backlog.description: As a Platform Engineer, I want a flexible and extensible plugin engine so that I can define and manage how technical debt KPIs are extracted from various build and test tools without modifying the core application code.

As a Platform Engineer, I want the Kronograf extractor to load and parse plugin definitions from both local files and URLs, as specified in `kronograf.yml`, so that I can define the set of active plugins for my project.
product_backlog.user_story: As a Platform Engineer, I want the Kronograf extractor to load and parse plugin definitions from both local files and URLs, so that I can define the set of active plugins for my project.
product_backlog.title: Load and Parse Plugin Definitions
acceptance_criteria: - Given a valid `kronograf.yml` file, when the extractor runs, then it correctly identifies and loads the plugins listed in the `plugins` section.
- Given a plugin is defined with a URL, when the extractor runs, then it downloads and caches the plugin file.
- Given a `kronograf.yml` file with plugin overrides, when the extractor runs, then the overridden rules are used instead of the default ones.

product_backlog.title: Parse Structured Reports
product_backlog.description: As a Plugin Author, I want to define KPI sources that use built-in parsers for common structured report formats (like JUnit XML, JaCoCo, etc.), so that I can extract data more robustly than with log scraping.
acceptance_criteria: - Given a JUnit XML report, when the extractor runs, then it correctly parses the number of tests.
- Given a JaCoCo XML report, when the extractor runs, then it correctly parses the test coverage percentage.
- Given an Android Lint XML report, when the extractor runs, then it correctly parses the number of lint errors and warnings.
- Given an OWASP Dependency-Check XML report, when the extractor runs, then it correctly parses the number of CVEs by severity.
product_backlog.user_story: As a Plugin Author, I want to define KPI sources that use built-in parsers for common structured report formats, so that I can extract data more robustly than with log scraping.

product_backlog.title: Implement Log Scraper with Versioned Rules
product_backlog.description: As a Plugin Author, I want to define KPI sources that use versioned, regex-based rules to scrape data from CI/CD build logs, so that I can extract KPIs when structured reports are not available.
product_backlog.user_story: As a Plugin Author, I want to define KPI sources that use versioned, regex-based rules to scrape data from CI/CD build logs, so that I can extract KPIs when structured reports are not available.
acceptance_criteria: - Given a log file and a set of plugin rules, when the extractor runs, then it correctly counts the number of lines matching a pattern (`count_matches`).
- Given a log file and a set of plugin rules, when the extractor runs, then it correctly extracts a numeric value from the first matching line (`extract_first`).
- Given a log file and a set of plugin rules, when the extractor runs, then it correctly extracts a numeric value from the last matching line (`extract_last`).
- Given a log file and a set of plugin rules, when the extractor runs, then it correctly sums numeric values from all matching lines (`extract_sum`).

product_backlog.title: Implement Git-based Data Store
product_backlog.summary: This epic covers the design and implementation of the data storage mechanism. For v1, this will be a dedicated Git branch within the same repository, holding an append-only NDJSON file. This approach is simple, requires no external infrastructure, and aligns with the Git-native philosophy of the tool.
product_backlog.description: As a Developer, I want to store the collected KPI data in a Git-native format, so that the data is versioned, auditable, and portable without requiring any external database or service.

product_backlog.title: Build the Android Kotlin Gradle Reference Plugin
product_backlog.summary: This epic covers the creation of the `android-kotlin-gradle` plugin. This plugin will be the primary example for the community and will exercise all the features of the plugin engine, including multiple structured report parsers and complex log scraping rules.
product_backlog.description: As a Plugin Author, I want a complete, production-ready reference plugin for a popular and complex ecosystem, so that I have a clear example of how to structure a plugin and what a good plugin looks like.

product_backlog.title: Create Static SVG Chart Generator
product_backlog.summary: This epic covers the creation of the static SVG chart generator. This component will read the data from the Git-based data store and produce clean, self-contained, and theme-aware SVG files for each tracked KPI.
product_backlog.description: As an Engineering Lead, I want to see the collected KPI data rendered as time-series SVG charts, so that I can embed them in my repository's README.md and easily communicate the state of our codebase's technical health to stakeholders.

product_backlog.title: Create Plugin Author CLI
product_backlog.summary: This epic covers the development of the `kronograf plugin` CLI. This tool will allow plugin authors to validate the syntax of their YAML files, run the sample assertions included in the plugin, and test the plugin against real build logs.
product_backlog.description: As a Plugin Author, I want a command-line interface (CLI) to validate and test my plugin definitions, so that I can be confident that my plugin is correct and will work as expected.

product_backlog.title: Create GitHub Actions Integration
product_backlog.summary: This epic covers the creation of a native GitHub Actions integration for Kronograf. This will make it easy for users to add Kronograf to their CI/CD pipeline with just a few lines of YAML.
product_backlog.description: As a DevOps Engineer, I want to integrate Kronograf into my GitHub Actions workflow, so that KPI data is collected and charts are updated automatically on every build.
As an Engineering Lead, I want to be able to generate historical KPI data for my existing repository, so that I can have a complete picture of my project's technical health from the very beginning.
product_backlog.title: Build Historical Backfill Tool
product_backlog.summary: This epic covers the development of the historical backfill tool. This tool will allow users to run the KPI extractor against previous commits in their repository, generating a complete historical record of their technical debt metrics.

acceptance_criteria: - Given a successful KPI extraction run, when the data store stage is executed, then a single JSON data point is appended to the `metrics.ndjson` file on the `kronograf-data` branch.
- Given the `kronograf-data` branch does not exist, when the data store stage is executed for the first time, then the branch is created.
- Given a CI/CD environment, when the data store stage is executed, then it uses the provided CI bot token to push the changes to the remote repository.
product_backlog.title: Append KPI Data to NDJSON File in Git Branch
product_backlog.user_story: As a Developer, I want to append KPI data to an NDJSON file on a dedicated Git branch, so that each CI run adds a new data point to the time-series.
product_backlog.description: As a Developer, I want to append KPI data to an NDJSON file on a dedicated Git branch, so that each CI run adds a new data point to the time-series.

product_backlog.epic_title: Build the Android Kotlin Gradle Reference Plugin
product_backlog.title: Extract Test Count and Coverage from Android/Gradle Build
product_backlog.user_story: As a Developer using Android, I want the reference plugin to extract test count and coverage, so I can track my project's testing state.
product_backlog.description: As a Developer using Android, Kotlin, and Gradle, I want the reference plugin to automatically extract the total number of tests and the overall test coverage percentage from my build artifacts, so that I can track the state of my project's testing.
acceptance_criteria: - Given a `kronograf.yml` file with the `android-kotlin-gradle` plugin enabled, when the extractor runs on a project with JUnit XML reports, then the `test_count` metric is correctly extracted.
- Given the extractor runs on a project with JaCoCo XML reports, then the `test_coverage_pct` metric is correctly extracted.
- Given the plugin is run against test reports from both unit tests and Android instrumented tests, then the metrics are correctly aggregated.

product_backlog.user_story: As an Android Developer, I want to extract build warnings and static analysis issues so that I can monitor code quality.
product_backlog.epic_title: Build the Android Kotlin Gradle Reference Plugin
product_backlog.description: As a Developer using Android, Kotlin, and Gradle, I want the reference plugin to extract the number of build warnings, Lint issues, and Detekt violations, so that I can monitor and drive down static analysis findings.
product_backlog.title: Extract Build Warnings and Static Analysis Issues from Android/Gradle Build
acceptance_criteria: - Given the `android-kotlin-gradle` plugin is enabled, when the extractor runs against a build log with Kotlin and Gradle warnings, then the `build_warnings` metric is correctly extracted and aggregated.
- Given the extractor runs against a project with Android Lint XML reports, then the `lint_errors` and `lint_warnings` metrics are correctly extracted.
- Given the extractor runs against a project that uses `detekt`, then the `detekt_issues` metric is correctly extracted from the build log.
- Given the build uses a version of the Kotlin compiler that changes the warning format, when the extractor runs, then the correct versioned rule is applied to parse the warnings.

product_backlog.title: Detect Tool Versions from Build Logs
product_backlog.user_story: As a Plugin Author, I want the plugin engine to automatically detect tool versions from the build log, so that the correct versioned rules are applied.
product_backlog.description: As a Plugin Author, I want the plugin engine to automatically detect the versions of tools from the build log, so that the correct versioned rules are applied without manual configuration.
acceptance_criteria: - Given a build log containing a recognizable version string for a tool (e.g., 'Gradle 8.9'), when the extractor runs, then it correctly identifies and stores the version number.
- Given a plugin rule with a `version_range` specified (e.g., '>=2.0.0'), when the engine has detected a matching tool version, then the rule is correctly selected for execution.
- Given a plugin rule with a `version_range` specified, when the engine has detected a tool version that does not match the range, then the rule is skipped.
- Given the engine cannot detect a tool version from the log, when a plugin has a fallback rule with `version_range: '*'`, then that rule is selected.

product_backlog.title: Aggregate Metric Values from Multiple Sources
acceptance_criteria: - Given a metric is configured with multiple `sources` (e.g., multiple JUnit XML file patterns), when the extractor runs, then the values from all sources are aggregated into a single metric value using the specified aggregation mode (e.g., `sum_tests`).
- Given a log-scraped metric is configured with multiple `rules`, when the extractor runs, then the values extracted by each rule are aggregated using the `multi_rule_aggregate` mode (e.g., `sum`).
- Given the configuration for a metric is invalid (e.g., an unknown `aggregate` mode is used), when the extractor runs, then it reports a clear error message.
product_backlog.user_story: As a Plugin Author, I want the plugin engine to aggregate values from multiple sources for a single metric, so that I can define comprehensive metrics.
product_backlog.description: As a Plugin Author, I want the plugin engine to aggregate values from multiple sources or rules for a single metric, so that I can define comprehensive metrics that cover an entire project.

As a Platform Engineer, I want to be able to activate and run multiple plugins concurrently in a single project, so that I can collect KPIs from different parts of my tech stack (e.g., frontend and backend).
acceptance_criteria: - Given `kronograf.yml` activates two or more different plugins, when the extractor runs, then it processes metrics from all active plugins.
- Given two active plugins define a metric with the same `id`, when the extractor runs, then it produces a clear warning or error about the conflict and does not silently overwrite data.

- Given a project uses both the built-in `android-kotlin-gradle` plugin and a custom plugin from a URL, when the extractor runs, then metrics from both plugins are collected and stored in the same data point.
product_backlog.user_story: As a Platform Engineer, I want to activate and run multiple plugins concurrently, so that I can collect KPIs from different parts of my tech stack.
product_backlog.title: Run Multiple Plugins Concurrently

product_backlog.user_story: As a Platform Engineer, I want to configure the data store settings in `kronograf.yml`, so that I can specify which branch to use for storing KPI data.
product_backlog.title: Configure Git-based Data Store
product_backlog.description: As a Platform Engineer, I want to configure the data store settings in `kronograf.yml`, so that I can specify which branch to use for storing KPI data.
acceptance_criteria: - Given a `kronograf.yml` file, when the `data_store` section is present, then the extractor uses the specified branch name (e.g., `kronograf-metrics`) instead of the default (`kronograf-data`).
- Given the `data_store` section specifies a `type` other than `git_branch`, when the extractor runs, then it produces a clear error message stating that only `git_branch` is supported in v1.0.
- Given the `data_store` section is absent from `kronograf.yml`, when the extractor runs, then it defaults to using the `git_branch` type and the `kronograf-data` branch name.

product_backlog.epic_title: Build the Android Kotlin Gradle Reference Plugin
product_backlog.user_story: As a Developer, I want the plugin to extract CVE counts from OWASP reports, so I can track and prioritize vulnerability remediation.
product_backlog.description: As a Security-conscious Developer, I want the reference plugin to extract the number of CVEs at different severity levels from OWASP Dependency-Check reports, so that I can track and prioritize vulnerability remediation efforts.
product_backlog.title: Extract CVE Counts from OWASP Dependency-Check Report
acceptance_criteria: - Given the `android-kotlin-gradle` plugin is enabled, when the extractor runs on a project with an OWASP Dependency-Check XML report, then the `cve_critical`, `cve_high`, and `cve_medium` metrics are correctly extracted based on CVSS scores.
- Given the OWASP report contains no vulnerabilities of a certain severity (e.g., no critical CVEs), then the corresponding metric is reported as 0.
- Given the OWASP report file is missing but configured in the plugin, when the extractor runs, then it logs a warning but does not fail the run, and reports the CVE metrics as 0 or null.
- Given the `android-kotlin-gradle` plugin is enabled, when the extractor runs against a build log that includes output from the `cloc` tool, then the `kotlin_loc` metric is correctly extracted.
- Given the `cloc` output shows zero lines of Kotlin code, then the metric is correctly reported as 0.
- Given the `cloc` output is not present in the build log, when the extractor runs, then it logs a warning but does not fail, and reports the `kotlin_loc` metric as null.
product_backlog.epic_title: Build the Android Kotlin Gradle Reference Plugin
product_backlog.user_story: As a Developer, I want the plugin to extract lines of Kotlin code from cloc output, so I can track codebase growth.
product_backlog.description: As a Developer, I want the reference plugin to extract the total lines of Kotlin code from the output of the `cloc` tool, so that I can track the growth of the codebase over time.
product_backlog.title: Extract Lines of Code from cloc Tool Output
